questions.stem: Where are the distress signals referred to in Rule 37 listed?
options: Annex I
Annex II
Annex III
Annex IV
questions.explanation: Rule 37 says a vessel in distress requiring assistance uses or exhibits the signals described in Annex IV. Annex I covers lights and shapes, Annex II the extra signals for fishing vessels fishing close together, and Annex III sound signal appliances.

questions.stem: Which two conditions does Rule 37 set for using distress signals?
options: The vessel is in distress and requires assistance
The vessel is over 12 metres and it is night
The vessel is in restricted visibility and not under command
The vessel has permission from the Coast Guard
questions.explanation: Rule 37 applies when a vessel is in distress and requires assistance. It has nothing to do with length, time of day or visibility, and no prior permission is needed to call for help.

questions.stem: A guest wants to fire an out-of-date red hand flare over the anchorage to celebrate a birthday. What does Annex IV say?
options: That is fine if the flare is expired
Distress signals must not be used except to indicate distress and need of assistance
That is fine if done before midnight
Only parachute flares are restricted
questions.explanation: Annex IV prohibits using any of its distress signals except to indicate distress and need of assistance, and also signals that might be confused with them. Expiry date, time of night and flare type make no difference: a red flare is read as distress.

questions.stem: Your engine has failed in a sheltered bay, the anchor is holding well and no one is hurt. You want a tow. Which is the best approach?
options: Fire red flares under Rule 37
Treat it as a routine call for assistance; it is not a distress situation
Sound continuous fog signals
Show a square flag with a ball above it
questions.explanation: Rule 37 is for a vessel in distress that requires assistance. Safely anchored with no one hurt, you are not in distress, so distress signals (red flares, continuous fog signal, flag and ball) would be wrong. Arrange a tow by ordinary means and stay alert in case the situation changes.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the difference between Rule 36 and Rule 37?
options: Rule 36 is for large vessels and Rule 37 for small ones
Rule 36 covers sound signals and Rule 37 covers light signals
They are two names for the same thing
Rule 36 covers signals to attract attention when not in distress; Rule 37 covers signals of distress and need of assistance
questions.explanation: Rule 36 lets any vessel attract attention with signals that cannot be confused with others. Rule 37 is specifically for a vessel in distress needing help, using the Annex IV signals. Both rules apply to all vessels and both include light and sound signals.
